_comment: Topology of the issue lifecycle axis: every node, the schema each edge carries, gates, failure policy and width budget. scripts/validate-workflow-graph.ts enforces it; see docs/adr/0003-workflow-graph-contract.md. runtime: conversational = needs mid-run human interaction, stays in the main agent; workflow = graphable island runnable as a Workflow script; chain = sequential and deliberately not a graph. Every registry entry carries its JSON Schema body: it is what `agent({schema})` enforces at runtime, what the markdown renderer builds the skill templates from, and it is self-contained (a $ref may only point into the entry's own $defs) because workflow scripts must inline it verbatim as `const SCHEMA_<Name> = {...}`, which is what the drift check reads. A workflow node whose island is built carries `script`: the repo-relative workflows/*.js file realising it (two sibling nodes may share one script — one island runs both). The contract is host-agnostic: an island is realisable as a Workflow script — Claude Code — or as Task + subagent orchestration over the same agents with `node scripts/island-reduce.ts` as the deterministic reducer — Cursor — emitting the same typed payloads; only the Workflow realisation carries the `script` binding. The binding arms the drift check in the omission direction: every schema in the node's `out` must be inlined in that script (rule 17) and each inline body must be a strict-JSON literal deep-equal to the registry body (rule 18). Inputs are deliberately exempt — they arrive through `args`, validated by their producer. A workflow node without `script` is an island not yet built. Irreversible actions on the axis are inventoried as `irreversible: true`: statuses-bind (creates tracker labels, tags or board columns), issue-write (creates the Linear issue), implement (pushes commits), close (merges the PR/MR and sets Done), auto-issue-mode (runs one issue from creation to merge on the user's single consent); each must sit behind a gate (rule 6). Gates carry the role split as data: a `decision` gate is the human's call — mechanism `tracker-status` or `chat-approval`, the Linear status being the only carrier of acceptance — while a `deny` gate is a hard prohibition that never asks, mechanism `pretooluse-hook` or `settings-deny`; the kind-mechanism pairing is a closed vocabulary (rule 19), so a new enforcement mechanism must change this contract deliberately. `frozenRules` is the first-class registry of frozen rules: a gate's `rule` points into it (rule 20), a deny gate exists only to enforce one (rule 21), and a rule no gate points to is rejected (rule 22). A frozen rule may carry `exemptions`: each names an existing node, the narrow scope it may touch despite the rule, and why (rule 23) — an exception written only in prose would be invisible to the check. `adapters` is the adapter contract: each key is an axis, a directory under `adapters/`; `config` names an enum property of a registry schema whose values are the legal adapter file names (`PlatformConfig.tracker`, `PlatformConfig.vcs`, `EntityPageUpdate.tier` for the vault axis, whose `file`/`mcp` value is the transport the skill's tier probe found rather than part of the platform config, and `Host.id` for the hosts axis, whose `grok-bot`/`claude-code`/`cursor` value is the runtime the skill's detect heuristic found rather than part of the platform config), and every adapter file must carry each required section as a line-start `## ` heading plus exactly the declared operation ids in the first column of its `## Operations` table — none missing, none twice, none undeclared (rule 24). A node that runs its skill through an axis names it in `adapters`, a non-empty array of declared axis keys; an unknown axis is rejected (rule 26). An axis may add `strategies`, naming the PlatformConfig enum of status strategies: its adapters must then carry a `## Status strategies` table listing exactly those strategies in the first column, each with both a read and a write recipe or `—` in both, and at least one supported (rule 25); what a strategy means is shared prose in `adapters/statuses.md`, and a real config is checked against its adapter by scripts/validate-platform-config.ts. An enum value without an adapter file is legal: the core skill stops with "adapter not available yet". Human gates sit on the boundaries between workflows, never inside them — the runtime takes no mid-run decision input (rule 8).

frozenRules.rule: Nothing is written to Linear before the user approves the drafted issue in chat.
No repo change — edit, build, install, commit, PR — before the issue is In Progress, a status only the human sets.

exemptions.scope: The `## Platform` section of the repo `CLAUDE.md`, replaced idempotently and nothing else in the repo.
exemptions.reason: Platform config is project setup, not issue work: it has to exist before any issue can be written, so it cannot wait for an issue to reach In Progress.

exemptions.scope: The `statuses` key inside the `## Platform` section of the repo `CLAUDE.md` — and, when the tracker is Azure DevOps Boards, the `team`, `board` and `workItemType` keys of its `ado` block, which name the board those statuses live on — replaced idempotently and nothing else in the repo.
exemptions.reason: The status binding decides how the in-progress gate itself is read, so it has to exist before the gate can hold — it cannot wait for an issue to pass that gate.

exemptions.scope: The one issue the run was invoked for: the run writes its `in-progress` phase itself, then branches, commits, pushes and opens the PR/MR for it; every other issue keeps the rule.
exemptions.reason: Invoking the skill is the user's explicit consent to the whole run, given in chat — it stands in for the human setting In Progress, and the rule holds unchanged outside that run.

exemptions.scope: The `in-progress` phase of the one issue it diagnosed, written with `issue.set-status` only when the next step is implementation and only after the user agrees in chat; the skill itself changes nothing in the repo — branch, commits and PR/MR stay with the skill it hands off to, and every other issue keeps the rule.
exemptions.reason: The user's explicit yes in chat stands in for setting In Progress by hand — the same approval `issue-workflow` already accepts as an explicit request to implement — and a refusal writes nothing.

frozenRules.rule: No label, tag or board column is created on the tracker without the user's explicit consent in chat.
No file outside the plan's affected files is changed without the user's consent in chat; after consent the file is added in a comment that extends the plan.

exemptions.scope: Files outside the plan's affected files of the one issue the run was invoked for, each added first in a comment that extends the plan with the reason; every other issue keeps the rule.
exemptions.reason: The run asks nothing after the drafted issue is approved; invoking it is the user's consent to the whole run, and the extending comment keeps the change visible on the tracker.

frozenRules.rule: No merge without green verification: tests and validators pass before close runs.

After a working session the Checkpoints entry on the entity page is mandatory in the same step as the Session summary comment. The only allowed skips are an unreachable vault (tier=none) or a project with no entity page, and those skips must be named in the Session summary — never silent. A Session summary without that write is not a finished session and is not a valid close-out.

schemas.description: The project's platform: which tracker holds its issues, which VCS host holds its code, and the identifiers each needs. Kept as the `## Platform` section of the repo `CLAUDE.md` and mirrored as `platform:` on the entity page; the tracker and vcs values name the adapter files core skills read.

tracker.title: Tracker
tracker.description: Where the project's issues live; `none` when the project has no tracker. Names the file under `adapters/trackers/`.

vcs.title: VCS host
vcs.description: Where the repo and its PRs/MRs live. Names the file under `adapters/vcs/`.

linear.title: Linear
linear.description: Linear identifiers, present when the tracker is Linear.

project.title: Project
project.description: Project UUID — stable across renames, unlike the name.

github.title: GitHub
github.description: GitHub identifiers, present when GitHub is the VCS host or the tracker.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: User or organisation owning the repo.

gitlab.title: GitLab
gitlab.description: GitLab identifiers, present when GitLab is the VCS host or the tracker.

ado.title: Azure DevOps
ado.description: Azure DevOps identifiers, present when Azure DevOps is the VCS host or the tracker.

team.title: Team
team.description: Team whose board carries the phases when Azure DevOps Boards is the tracker; written by `bind-statuses`, required under the `native` strategy.

board.title: Board
board.description: That team's board, named after its backlog level (e.g. `Stories`); its columns are the `native` status values.

workItemType.title: Work item type
workItemType.description: Type new issues are created as (e.g. `User Story`) — one the board carries.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: How the tracker shows the five canonical phases, written by `bind-statuses`. Optional: absent, the tracker adapter's `## Statuses` default applies.

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.description: Where a phase lives on the tracker: its own state field, a label plus open/closed, or a `Status: <value>` marker comment. Each tracker adapter lists its recipe per strategy in `## Status strategies`.

map.title: Status map
map.description: Phase → value: state names for `native`, label names or the reserved `open`/`closed` for `label`, marker values for `comment`. No value is mapped twice.

backlog.title: Backlog
backlog.description: A filed issue nobody has planned yet.

todo.title: Todo
todo.description: The implementation plan is posted and waits for the human.

in-progress.title: In progress
in-progress.description: The human approved the plan; only the human writes this phase.

in-review.title: In review
in-review.description: The change is up for code review.

done.title: Done
done.description: The work is merged or the human closed the issue.

schemas.description: The filed issue: objective, scope, acceptance criteria, constraints.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: One or two sentences: the outcome we want and for whom. Testable, not a task list.

problemAndContext.title: Problem & context
problemAndContext.description: Why now? What's broken / missing / requested. Link related issues or docs.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Acceptance criteria
acceptanceCriteria.description: Each item independently verifiable and ending with how it is checked — a test name or a command, written as `— check: <test or command>`. A criterion that cannot name its check is too vague and goes back to the spec. This is what "done" means.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Both halves matter: the out list is what stops the issue growing during planning.

outOfScope.title: Out of scope
outOfScope.description: What it deliberately leaves to another issue — a different topic, never this issue's own implementation (not "implementacja w osobnym issue" / "implementation in a separate issue").

constraints.title: Constraints
constraints.description: Tech constraints, non-functional requirements, deadlines, compatibility. Omit if none.

dependencies.title: Dependencies / related
dependencies.description: Blocking issues, external prerequisites, related TEAM-123 ids. Omit if none.

implementationChecklist.title: Implementation checklist
implementationChecklist.description: Use ONLY when the work is one deliverable with clear steps and is NOT split into sub-issues. If split into sub-issues, drop this section.

openQuestions.title: Open questions
openQuestions.description: Anything still ambiguous the planner/implementer must resolve. Omit if none.

schemas.description: Vault recall for the project: entity page sections, decisions, 1-hop graph.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: Slug of the entity page the SessionStart hook injected.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.description: Recorded project decisions the plan must not contradict without flagging it.

activeContext.title: Active context
activeContext.description: What the entity page says is currently in flight.

relatedPages.title: Related pages
relatedPages.description: One hop out: pages linked from the entity page or linking back to it.

schemas.description: The in-repo half of the plan context, gathered in parallel: repo layout, prior plans, related issues, ADRs. The vault half travels separately as ProjectContext, because a node belongs to exactly one skill.

repoLayout.title: Repo layout
repoLayout.description: The directories and files the change will touch.

conventions.title: Conventions
conventions.description: In-repo rules the plan must follow: CONTEXT.md terms, ADRs, commit style.

priorArt.title: Prior art
priorArt.description: Earlier plans, related issues and merged PRs worth reading before drafting.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description: Test, build and validator commands the plan will cite.

stats.title: Fan-out stats
stats.description: Passive observability of the fan-out, counted by the reducer from what the run already produced. Optional: absent whenever the context was gathered sequentially instead of as an island.

gatherers.title: Per gatherer
gatherers.description: One row per gatherer the island spawns, in its fixed spawn order — a failed gatherer stays in the list with zeros rather than vanishing.

items.title: Gatherer stats
items.description: What one gatherer contributed to the reduced context.

source.title: Source
source.description: The gatherer this row counts, e.g. `conventions`.

returned.title: Returned
returned.description: Non-empty list items the gatherer returned, before reduction.

unique.title: Unique
unique.description: Items it was the first to contribute that survived into the reduced context. A gatherer at zero across successive runs is a removal candidate.

duplicatesDropped.title: Duplicates dropped
duplicatesDropped.description: Returned items the reducer discarded as duplicates or past a recall limit — the fan-out's redundancy.

gapsCount.title: Gaps
gapsCount.description: Gaps the run reported: the node-failure count for this island.

schemas.description: The plan posted to Linear as a `## Implementation plan` comment.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: One paragraph: what problem we solve and for whom.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Both halves matter: the out list is what stops the work growing mid-implementation.

outOfScope.title: Out of scope
outOfScope.description: What it deliberately leaves to another issue — a different topic, never this issue's own implementation (not "implementacja w osobnym issue" / "implementation in a separate issue").

technicalApproach.title: Technical Approach
technicalApproach.description: Architecture / strategy, and why this one over the alternatives.

affectedFiles.title: Affected Files
affectedFiles.description: Every file or directory the implementation will change. Changing anything outside this list needs the user's consent in chat, and the file is then added in a comment that extends the plan.

items.title: Affected file
items.description: A file or directory and what happens to it.

file.title: File
file.description: Repo-relative path of a file or directory.

change.title: Change
change.description: What the plan does to it: new, edited, regenerated, removed.

implementationSteps.title: Implementation Steps
implementationSteps.description: Ordered steps, each one an atomic commit.

testApproach.title: Test approach
testApproach.description: How the implementation is driven. TDD is the default; leaving it is allowed, never silent: the reason stands here, is approved together with the move to In Progress, and is carried into the session summary.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: TDD runs nerd4rent:tdd; no tests is a plain implementation backed by the reason below.

seams.title: Seams
seams.description: The public boundaries the tests will be written against: a function, a CLI, a contract. Decided here, not asked mid-implementation.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Required when the mode is no tests: why, and the nearest runnable check that stands in for a test. Under TDD, what is deliberately left untested, if anything.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Acceptance Criteria
acceptanceCriteria.description: Each item independently verifiable and ending with how it is checked — a test name or a command. This is what closes the issue.

risks.title: Risks
risks.description: One row per risk, each with the mitigation that keeps it survivable.

mitigation.title: Mitigation
mitigation.description: What keeps it from sinking the work.

dependencies.title: Dependencies
dependencies.description: Blocking issues, tooling and prerequisites outside this plan.

schemas.description: Commits pushed to the issue branch plus the draft PR that tracks them.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: The issue branch the commits landed on.

commits.title: Commits
commits.description: One line per commit, in the order they were pushed.

pullRequest.title: Pull request
pullRequest.description: URL of the draft PR carrying the Linear magic word.

validation.title: Validation
validation.description: Commands run against the change and what they reported.

criteriaVerification.title: Criteria verification
criteriaVerification.description: One row per acceptance criterion of the spec, filled before the move to review. A single `fail` blocks that move.

items.title: Criterion check
items.description: One acceptance criterion and the evidence that it holds.

criterion.title: Criterion
criterion.description: The acceptance criterion as the spec states it.

check.title: Check
check.description: The test or command that was run for it.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: What the check reported: a test count, an exit code, the line that proves it.

schemas.description: The review request confirmed in review-menu: the change range to read. The four review axes are fixed and always all run, so the request carries no axis list.

range.title: Change range
range.description: The diff range to read, e.g. `main...HEAD`.

schemas.description: Verified findings plus the stats that make degradation visible. Every finding survived adversarial verification: 3 independent sceptics each try to refute it, and 2 or more refutations out of 3 reject it; rejected findings never reach this payload, but their count does. When verified findings from different axes share one file:line anchor, a judge decides which takes precedence; an overruled finding leaves `findings` but stays verbatim in `conflicts`. A single finding never travels an edge on its own, so ReviewFinding lives as a `$defs` inside this entry.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One paragraph: what the review covered and whether the change is ready.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: One row per finding that survived verification.

stats.title: Stats
stats.description: Degradation made visible: what each stage let through, so a silent drop is impossible.

mapped.title: Mapped
mapped.description: Raw findings the axis mappers returned, before reduction.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.description: Findings refuted by 2 or more of the 3 sceptics.

unverifiedOverflow.title: Unverified overflow
unverifiedOverflow.description: Findings that never got a verdict: past the verification cap, or with fewer than 2 votes cast.

overruled.title: Overruled
overruled.description: Verified findings the judge set aside in favour of another axis on the same anchor; each one is kept verbatim in conflicts.

conflicts.title: Conflicts
conflicts.description: One row per anchor where verified findings from different axes collided and the judge gave a valid verdict; empty when no axes collided.

AxisConflict.title: Axis conflict
AxisConflict.description: Verified findings from different axes on one file:line, and the judge's verdict on which takes precedence.

file.title: File
file.description: Repo-relative path of the shared anchor.

axes.title: Axes
axes.description: The axes whose findings collided, in arrival order.

prevails.title: Prevails
prevails.description: The axis whose finding takes precedence, or both when the findings do not contradict each other and all stay. A security finding is never overruled: when security is among the axes, any verdict other than security or both is invalid, so every finding stays and the conflict becomes a gap.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: The judge's one- or two-sentence justification.

overruled.title: Overruled
overruled.description: The findings set aside, verbatim; empty when the verdict is both.

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: The review axis that raised the finding.

file.title: File
file.description: Repo-relative path the finding sits in.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Concrete inputs or state that make the claim fail — what makes it checkable.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How much damage it does if left in.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure the verification pass is that the finding is real: high only when all 3 sceptics cast a vote and none refuted; medium when one refuted or a sceptic returned no vote.

schemas.description: The `## Session summary` comment: what changed, what remains, validation, next steps, and the Checkpoint field that names the entity-page write or an explicit skip.

changed.title: What changed
changed.description: Files and areas touched in this session.

remaining.title: Scope remaining
remaining.description: What is still open, so the next session can resume from Linear alone.

status.title: Current status
status.description: Where the work stands and what the issue status is.

validation.title: Validation
validation.description: Commands run and what they reported — evidence, not assertions.

testApproach.title: Test approach
testApproach.description: The mode the session implemented in, taken from the plan. Omit when the session implemented nothing.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The mode from the plan's test approach.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Under no tests: the plan's reason and the stand-in check that was actually run, with its result. Also when the plan carried no test approach and the mode was assumed.

criteriaVerification.title: Criteria verification
criteriaVerification.description: The criteria table from the change set, once implementation is complete: one row per acceptance criterion, check, result and evidence. Omit while implementation is still in progress.

items.title: Criterion check
items.description: One acceptance criterion and the evidence that it holds.

criterion.title: Criterion
criterion.description: The acceptance criterion as the spec states it.

check.title: Check
check.description: The test or command that was run for it.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: What the check reported: a test count, an exit code, the line that proves it.

nextSteps.title: Open questions / next steps
nextSteps.description: What the next session should pick up, and what is still undecided.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: One line per figure the run already produced — `PlanContext.stats`, the gaps an island reported, the verifier rejection rate. Passive by construction: nothing is measured that the run did not emit anyway, and the comment is the only place it is stored. Omit when no island ran.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Vault path of the entity page that received the Checkpoints entry in this same step, or an explicit skip: `skipped: tier=none` or `skipped: no entity page`. A Session summary without this field is an incomplete failed step — not a finished session and not a green light for personal-docs or close.

schemas.description: The user's guide in the nerdbrain vault that the close-out waits for: the guide written or updated for the issue, or the one-line reason none was written. The caller of the close-out produces it on the session model (issue-workflow's close-out, auto-issue-mode's close-out stage) and records it as a `## Personal guide` issue comment; issue-close only checks it in the vault or that comment and stops without it.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: What the step did: the guide was written or updated, the work needs no guide, or the machine has no vault.

path.title: Path
path.description: Vault path of the guide, `5-wiki/guides/{topic}.md`; present when a guide was written or updated.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One line on why no guide was written; present when none was.

links.title: Links
links.description: The issue, PR and commit links the guide's history section received.

schemas.description: The merged PR/MR, the checkout switched to the base branch, the issue set to Done.

pullRequest.title: Pull request
pullRequest.description: The merged PR/MR and the commit it landed as.

baseBranch.title: Base branch
baseBranch.description: The branch the local checkout switched to after the merge.

issueState.title: Issue state
issueState.description: The Linear state the issue was left in.

schemas.description: The entity page edit plus the index/log upkeep that goes with it.

page.title: Page
page.description: Vault path of the entity page that was written.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: Which sections were edited or appended, and in which mode.

upkeep.title: Index and log upkeep
upkeep.description: The `index.md` / `log.md` lines added alongside the page edit.

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: The vault transport the write went through, as the skill's tier probe found it. Names the file under `adapters/vault/`; `none` has no adapter because nothing is written.

schemas.description: The agent host running this session, as the skill's detect heuristic found it. Names the file under `adapters/hosts/`. Not part of the platform config and not an island payload: a repo does not know which host will open it, and auto-issue-mode never reads this axis.

id.title: Host
id.description: Which agent runtime is running this session. Names the file under `adapters/hosts/`. Selected by env and the session's tool list, the way grill picks an ask tool; `none` of the signals falls through to `claude-code`.

failure.fallback: stop and ask the user; the adapter default statuses keep applying

gates.description: The user confirms the status map, and separately each label, tag or board column to create on the tracker, before anything is written there.
The user approves the drafted issue before anything is written to Linear.

failure.fallback: continue without vault context and flag the gap in the plan
degrade to the sequential context read in the main agent

gates.description: For a complex issue the planner refines the description to the full IssueSpec variant; the user accepts the new text in chat before `issue.update-description` writes it.
The human sets the issue to In Progress in Linear; no repo change happens before that.
Before changing a file outside the plan's affected files the agent stops, names the file and the reason, and continues only after the user's yes in chat.
A spec change after work has started: the user accepts the new description in chat before it is written, together with a `## Spec change` comment saying what changed and why.

failure.fallback: fall back to the user reviewing the PR manually

gates.description: The user confirms the change range the four axes will review; the runtime takes no mid-run input, so this cannot move inside review-verify.

failure.fallback: report partial findings and mark the run incomplete
stop before issue-close and report; a machine without the vault reports no-vault instead of failing, and issue-close refuses to merge while the guide is missing
stop and report (merge conflict, missing gh/glab)

gates.description: The human asks to close, or sets the issue to Done with the PR still open; the merge is irreversible.

The human asks to close, or sets the issue to Done with the PR still open; close-out does not run until wiki-write has written the Checkpoints entry or recorded an explicit skip (tier=none or no entity page). A Session summary comment alone is not a finished session and not a valid close-out.

failure.fallback: stop and report: a reachable vault with an entity page must receive the Checkpoints entry; only an unreachable vault (tier=none) or a project with no entity page may skip, and that skip is named in the Session summary — never silent
stop and report what is done, what is pending, the exact error and how to resume from the issue ID

gates.description: The user approves the drafted issue before it is written to the tracker — the run's single human stop, skipped when it resumes an existing issue ID.

Invoking the skill in chat is the user's decision to close, taken up front in place of asking to close or setting Done; the merge still runs only after tests and validators are green, and red verification stops the run.

failure.fallback: stop and report the phase read, the evidence gathered and the exact error; nothing is written

gates.description: The user agrees in chat to move the issue to In Progress when the next step is implementation; a refusal ends the skill with nothing written, and the repo change itself waits for the skill it hands off to.
